subject: Surge bridging credit and rate-tier path for Q2 launch
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina@quickcart.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week surge — need rate-tier guidance and temporary credit

Hi Priyom,

We're ramping into our feature launch the week of June 3 and expect an initial burst of inference traffic for the checkout flow (estimated 40–60M tokens/day for ~72 hours). Our current committed tier won't cover it and procurement flagged potential overrun costs as a blocker for sign-off.

Questions: can you outline options for a short-term rate-tier upgrade (S1 -> S2) vs. a one-time burst credit? We need (1) a hard cap on spend if we hit X tokens/day, (2) timing for provisioning, and (3) how you handle true-ups at month end.

Would love a brief proposal by Monday so we can finalize the PO.

Thanks,
Nina Patel
Head of Product
QuickCart

--
Attachment: traffic_projection_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@quickcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week surge — need rate-tier guidance and temporary credit

Hi Nina — thanks for the heads up and the projection. Short answer: yes, we can do both a rate-tier bump and a temporary burst credit.

Proposal (high level):
- Short-term rate-tier upgrade: move from S1 to S2 for a 7-day window. Immediate effect, prorated daily charge. Can be provisioned within 24 hours of approval.
- Burst bridging credit: Redwood grants a one-time credit equal to 50% of estimated overrun charges up to a cap of $18,000 for this event (applies only to token overrun, not reserved capacity fees).
- True-up: consumption above committed levels during the month is invoiced then offset by the credit. Outstanding net overrun is billed on next invoice; we can amortize if requested but would need procurement sign-off.

I'll attach a detailed breakdown and a two-option pricing table (S2 tier cost vs. payg with credit). Opening to adjust the credit cap if you can commit to a 3-month minimum or a committed headroom in Q3.

Attached: QuickCart_burst_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal with numbers)

If that works I can loop in Vanessa to approve the credit and Marcus to verify provisioning lead time.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: QuickCart_burst_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week surge — need rate-tier guidance and temporary credit

Looping in Vanessa for formal credit approval. A couple of notes from a margin / precedent perspective:
- 50% credit up to $18k is reasonable for a single short event but request we make the credit conditional on a two-month committed ARR cliff (or an agreed evaluation checkpoint).
- Recommend adding a hard spend ceiling for the event (QuickCart signals a preferred cap of $25k/day; we should formalize).
- For true-up handling, Finance prefers to net at invoice rather than amortize without a signed agreement. If QuickCart can provide a PO with the expected headroom, we can expedite provisioning.

Also, Marcus — please confirm if ops can spin S2 within 24 hours for a named customer and whether there are any region constraints for our us-west cluster.

-Jordan
Director, Sales Operations
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week surge — need rate-tier guidance and temporary credit

We can provision S2 for QuickCart in us-west within 24 hours. Two operational items:
- We will need a confirmed API key and account ID to pin routing to S2 nodes.
- If token throughput exceeds 80M tokens/day sustained for >12 hours, autoscaling will trigger burst instances billed at pay-as-you-go rates — that will be included in the overrun calculation.

No region constraints. Ops recommends a 6-hour warmup prior to peak to preload KV caches and avoid cold-start latency spikes. Happy to take a short call with QuickCart's infra team.

-Marcus
Head of Platform Reliability
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@quickcart.com>, procurement@quickcart.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: S2 upgrade + one-time credit — action and PO request

Nina — per our proposal attached:
- Redwood will provision an S2 rate-tier upgrade for QuickCart starting June 3 for a 7-day window (provisioning contingent on PO).
- One-time bridging credit: 50% of estimated overrun charges up to $18,000. Applies only to token overrun beyond current commitments.
- Hard spend cap: $25,000/day unless you request otherwise in the PO. If actual consumption exceeds the cap we will contact you before any additional spend is incurred.

Next steps for QuickCart to confirm:
1) Send PO to procurement@redwood.ai referencing deal QC-2026-045 and noting the agreed S2 start date and spend cap.
2) Provide account ID and API key to ops@redwood.ai for provisioning.
3) If you'd like the credit changed to a different structure (lower cap + multi-month commit), tell me and we can discuss a tailored contract amendment.

Attaching the proposal and the redline-ready MA for procurement.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

-Priyom

--
Attachments: QuickCart_burst_proposal_v3.pdf; signed_MA_proposal_redlines.docx
From: Nina Patel <nina@quickcart.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quickcart.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: S2 upgrade + one-time credit — action and PO request

Priyom — thanks, this looks good. Procurement will issue a PO today referencing QC-2026-045 and the $25k/day cap. We'll send account details and an API key to ops@redwood.ai once the PO is in flight.

Quick note: procurement asked if the credit can be applied before invoice (i.e., we see reduced estimated charges on the staging invoice) — happy to have Finance/Procurement sync with Vanessa if needed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Product, QuickCart
